item.title: Manchester City appeal guilty verdict over Premier League financial breaches
item.description: Manchester City have lodged an appeal after an independent commission found the club guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations. The club says the commission's ruling contains what it describes as clear errors of law, principle and fact, and maintains it has evidence supporting its position.
item.content:encoded:
Manchester City have lodged an appeal after an independent commission found the club guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.

The club says the commission's ruling contains what it describes as clear errors of law, principle and fact, and maintains it has evidence supporting its position.

City were found guilty of breaching financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

The independent panel found that City arranged what it described as sham contracts with several commercial partners to disguise more than FJ$2.46 billion in secret funding.

The Premier League says the club systematically broke its rules for nearly a decade.

Meanwhile, the Football Association says the verdict has significant implications for the integrity of the game and it is considering the decision and what action may be required.

Proceedings between Manchester City and the Premier League remain ongoing.

item.title: Bula Boys eye MSG Prime Minister’s Cup title against Vanuatu
item.description: The Fiji Bula Boys will be looking to turn the tables on Vanuatu when the two sides meet in the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup 2026 final tomorrow. The Bula Boys aim to finish the tournament on a high in front of their home fans.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Bula Boys will be looking to turn the tables on Vanuatu when the two sides meet in the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup 2026 final tomorrow.

The Bula Boys aim to finish the tournament on a high in front of their home fans.

The two teams have already met in the round-robin stage, where Vanuatu defeated Fiji 1-0.

T hat result means Fiji will head into the final knowing the challenge Vanuatu poses as they look to claim the regional title.

Fans are being encouraged to turn out in numbers to support the teams at the HFC Bank Stadium.

Fiji will face Vanuatu at 4pm tomorrow at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva.

The women’s final between Papua New Guinea and Vanuatu will be played at 12pm.

item.description: Rewa FC defender Delon Shankar and Labasa FC midfielder Melvin Mani may not be taking part in the FMF Inter District Championship as they have been suspended. Speaking to fijivillage News Fiji Football Association Chief Executive Officer Mohammed Yusuf says Mani was suspended after he failed to return to camp following the BOG tournament and did not report for national team duties.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa FC defender Delon Shankar and Labasa FC midfielder Melvin Mani may not be taking part in the FMF Inter District Championship as they have been suspended.

Speaking to fijivillage News Fiji Football Association Chief Executive Officer Mohammed Yusuf says Mani was suspended after he failed to return to camp following the BOG tournament and did not report for national team duties.

Yusuf says Shankar was released from the national team camp to undergo rehabilitation but instead travelled to New Zealand.

He says Shankar is currently in New Zealand and has not been allowed to play.

Yusuf says both players remain suspended indefinitely until the Fiji FA Board makes a decision.

He says the timing of the Board meeting will depend on when the Board can meet, as the IDC will be held next week, and the matter will be discussed if an appeal is lodged.
